correctness.rationale: A connected weighted tree satisfies tr(L^+)=(1/N)sum_e s_e(N-s_e)/w_e, giving strict convexity in each individually adjustable positive transition probability. Root/branch row caps reduce the unconstrained global minimizer to strictly convex A/x+B/(1-x), x<=1/k. The unique optimum is x=min(1/k,sqrt(a)/(sqrt(a)+m sqrt(b))) and y=(1-x)/m. Exact polynomial identities F_k(k^2-3k+4)=4 and F_k(k^2-3k+3)=3-k(k^2-3k+4)<0 prove the integer cutoff for all k>=2; positive-root uniqueness follows from a negative constant coefficient and positive leading coefficient. The two asymptotic limits and equal-edge regret follow from explicit leading terms. A standard-library verifier passed 1484 diagnostics, including independent Laplacian inversions, but infinite correctness rests on the proof.

value.rationale: The exact active-set transition k^2-3k+4 identifies where a globally Kemeny-optimal uniform-stationary walk should begin spending holding probability at a root, while the branch children remain nonlazy. This is a natural structural design decision on a two-level network, not an arbitrary finite table. The nondegenerate quadratic scaling crossover (1-rho^-1/2)_+ and the limiting equal-edge cost factor 2-1/k quantify why the specific exact threshold matters in large networks; no arbitrary-general-graph theorem is claimed.
